name: re0
when: An existing artifact has stale content, accumulated patches, or nearby documents that must stay aligned.
note: Read the whole artifact, preserve useful detail, and change nothing when no improvement is warranted.

name: readchk
when: A request or delegated brief is substantial, bundled, ambiguous, or costly to misunderstand.
note: Resolve meaning from available context silently; ask only about a surviving fork. Record one understood-as line for substantial work.

name: aim
when: The user hands over material without a sufficiently formed request.
note: Read the material and propose the likely intent for confirmation. Do not replace an already clear request with a new confirmation step.

name: modelchk
when: Before a substantial work unit or when risk, ambiguity, verification cost, or failed attempts change its required capability or effort.
note: Recommend a neutral tier and effort with rationale, escalation/de-escalation triggers, and proof surface. Only the workflow executor selects a configured concrete model and actual effort level.

name: hate
when: The user explicitly requests this adversarial attack on a plan, design, or argument.
note: Return the single load-bearing objection and its cheapest falsification, not an automatic demolition pass or a checklist.

name: macrothink
when: The user explicitly requests independent fresh reads to challenge the current direction's framing.
note: Lead owns 2-5 context-free read-only runs, default 3, through the bounded job queue. Report divergence first; same-model agreement is not proof.

name: feynman
when: The user explicitly asks to test their understanding of a just-made decision.
note: Use a fresh critic and ask the user one gap at a time. This is an interactive learning exercise, not an automatic implementation gate.

name: autobahn
when: Actual risk-adjacent scope needs an explicit safe alternative before execution.
note: Use only safe scope in a context-clean job, with one independent re-sweep. Preserve actual safety constraints and existing authorization; resolve scope-changing gray areas before execution. Never use isolation to evade safeguards or run this on every ordinary task.

name: reorder
when: The user explicitly requests an intentional order for a listing, table, catalog, sections, or enum.
note: Move existing items only under one stated principle; do not reword, add, or remove them. Keep mirrored listings aligned.

name: detool
when: An artifact promises portability or cross-agent reuse but contains incidental stack-specific mechanisms.
note: Keep runbooks, exact commands, provenance, measured limits, and claims about a named tool concrete.

name: dedash
when: The user explicitly requests removing em-dash constructions in a named prose scope.
note: Judge each occurrence in context; preserve ranges, code, identifiers, quotes, and the user's scope.

name: debloat
when: The user explicitly requests compressing correct but verbose prose while preserving its meaning.
note: Preserve every load-bearing claim and useful teaching detail. Route stale content to re0 and cross-file duplication to ssotize.

name: shower
when: An important artifact or handoff must make sense without the author's accumulated session context.
note: A real fresh context reads only the artifact contents, never the author's intent or neighboring project files. Child roles request the cold-read through Lead instead of spawning their own orchestration.

name: factchk
when: A factual claim about the outside world, a product, a source, a number, or novelty lacks checked evidence.
note: Use reachable external primary sources and cite them; report unavailable evidence instead of guessing. Review roles return findings, while the authorized author fixes mechanically clear errors.

name: mandela
when: A test, eval, benchmark, metric, or experiment may validate its own assumptions without independent ground truth.
note: Audit read-only for the upstream eight leakage patterns. High-stakes designs may request one additional fresh auditor through Lead.

name: sip
when: A changed artifact is ready for completion, review, or handoff.
note: Select applicable model-invoked checks: shower, factchk or mandela, ssotize audit, conditional detool, and re0. Reuse evidence for an unchanged artifact revision, record skips, and never commit or start a second top-level loop.

name: re0-git
when: The user explicitly asks to clean up the message of an existing commit.
note: Changes history, not the tree, and requires signing support. Never create a commit because this skill is available; rewriting pushed/shared history needs explicit authorization.

name: re0-release
when: The user explicitly invokes the Paperthin release procedure for a project that adopts its required release conventions.
note: The upstream procedure is tied to Paperthin catalogs, signed tags, and release CI. Inspect applicability and existing authorization; do not impose its checklist on an unrelated target project or infer publishing permission from skill installation.

name: re0-merge
when: The user explicitly invokes the Paperthin contribution-landing procedure for a compatible project.
note: Preserve contributor authorship and the target project's actual merge policy. PR reviews, comments, and remote changes require their own existing authorization. Do not auto-invoke other user-only skills mentioned by the upstream procedure.

name: ssotize
when: A particular fact is duplicated, scattered, stale, or contradictory across artifacts.
note: Start with a read-only two-method audit. Review roles stay audit-only. Execute a concrete consolidation plan only with user authorization; preserve unique details and surface contradictions.

name: re0-upgrade
when: The user explicitly asks to maintain a separate Paperthin installation managed by npx skills.
note: This Pi package vendors a pinned catalog and updates through pi update. Its absence from npx skills is not a missing install. Do not add a duplicate installation, modify hooks, or star a repository automatically.

name: re0-plan
when: The user explicitly requests the Paperthin repository's iteration casebook convention.
note: Upstream explicitly calls this paperthin-only and not portable: it assumes the full suite and .re0/iteration lifecycle. Never use it as an implicit generic project planner or start a parallel workflow directory.

name: re0-loop
when: A long project needs repeated build, real-surface QA, and evidence-backed learning cycles.
note: Lead owns the only active orchestration loop. Fit re0-memo, optional nba, and justified re0-work into the current task's phases. Stop internal laps when no outside evidence enters; children must not start nested loops.

name: re0-memo
when: A phase, attempt, QA run, or user feedback reveals a reusable lesson or a failure class for the next pass.
note: Record evidence-backed lessons and next gates in the current task's local artifacts; preserve failed paths and avoid adding process history to the shipped product.

name: re0-work
when: Evidence shows the foundation is wrong and a controlled restart is better than another patch.
note: Make the preserve/discard split explicit, archive negative evidence, and test the first replacement slice in an isolated worktree when appropriate. This never grants permission to destroy existing work or spawn a nested lead.

name: catchup
when: The user returns after a gap, loses the thread, or needs an explanation of newly introduced project terms.
note: Brief from live files, git state, and recorded evidence; explain decisions needed before chronology. Do not act while presenting the briefing.

name: nba
when: The active workflow is between phases, blocked by too many options, or needs a state-grounded next move.
note: Return exactly one action with why-now and done-when. It recommends without executing; Lead retains transition ownership and user-only skills remain explicit.

name: prism
when: The user explicitly requests independent lenses because the artifact has genuinely different failure modes.
note: Choose 2-5 distinct lenses, run bounded read-only jobs, and return the disagreement and resolving question. Do not equate more reviewers or majority agreement with proof.
